bridgeRouteRisk.summary: wiTRY uses LayerZero OFT Adapter infrastructure between Ethereum and MegaETH. Brix docs list an Ethereum wiTRY OFT Adapter and a MegaETH wiTRY OFT representation bridged through LayerZero messaging, so the route is external lock/mint rather than MegaETH canonical rollup bridging. Pinned owner reads on 2026-10-01 distinguish the immediate owners: Ethereum wiTRY is owned by contract 0x15bf1ac31c5b8c0e0960d656de02ba5593b19c47, whose owner is Brix Safe 0x7ac3bb10225a4ef27134bcf54454d545a1738662; MegaETH wiTRY is owned directly by that Safe. The former uniform-immediate-owner description is no longer current.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Kimi P2 control cohort dc-1 (lead usdt-tether)

routes.reviewNote: Historical 2026-07-20 review recorded the Brix Safe as immediate owner. At Ethereum block 26095937 on 2026-10-01, symbol() = wiTRY and decimals() = 18, while owner() = contract 0x15bf1ac31c5b8c0e0960d656de02ba5593b19c47. That contract's owner() = Brix Safe 0x7ac3bb10225a4ef27134bcf54454d545a1738662. Native issuance remains on Ethereum; the immediate owner is now an intermediate contract rather than the terminal Safe.

Historical 2026-07-20 review recorded symbol wiTRY and 18 decimals. At MegaETH block 28042374 on 2026-10-01, owner() still returned Brix Safe 0x7ac3bb10225a4ef27134bcf54454d545a1738662. This differs from Ethereum wiTRY's current immediate owner, contract 0x15bf1ac31c5b8c0e0960d656de02ba5593b19c47. Current peer, messaging-security and bridge-mint authorization state are not established by the owner read alone.
